title: KV cache adviser: hit-rate forecasting, TTL policy generator, and safe rollout guardrails
creator: Diego Ramirez
description: Problem: We have a variety of workloads with different prefix/token distributions and current TTL heuristics are hand-tuned causing inconsistent hit-rate improvements and occasional regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. Goal: Build a KV Cache Adviser service that (1) forecasts per-route and per-tenant cache hit-rate under candidate key designs and TTLs, (2) synthesizes recommended TTL/policy profiles (including shard/key-normalization suggestions and suggested batching windows), and (3) provides a safe apply/rollback orchestration that can perform staged rollout, automated rollback on specified KPIs, and a safety dry-run mode for Prod config preview. Scope: MVP for hosted API routes and Dedicated pools (target endpoints: text-generation and chat routes). Out of scope for MVP: embedding cache advisory and on-prem private control plane automation (to be considered in next phase). Success metrics: average cross-tenant cost-per-token reduction of >=12% on test cohort, false-positive regression rate (recommendation that causes >5% latency or quality regression after rollout) < 2%, and adviser-synth recommendations accepted by SRE/product 4/5 times in first 50 trials.
acceptance_criteria: Adviser produces per-route CSV of forecasted hit-rate vs TTL for 1,7,30 day horizons and a ranked list of recommended TTLs and key-normalizations
A simulated rollout framework that replays historical traffic and validates recommendations against a held-out 2-week window producing predicted impact on tokens_served and p95 latency
Safe apply flow implemented: canary (1% traffic) -> ramp (10% -> 50%) -> full, with automated rollback triggers on p95 latency > baseline+15% or error_rate spike > baseline*3
Operational dashboard surfaced in Console showing recommendation, projected cost savings, canary results, and a single-click rollback
Unit and e2e tests for forecasting model with coverage for seasonality and prefix cold-start scenarios
tasks: Design forecasting model: baseline EWMA + seasonal decomposition experiment, and prototype an LSTM baseline for comparison
Schema for candidate cache policies and key-normalizations (include tokenization-aware keys, prefix-hash sharding, and canonicalization rules)
Implement simulator that replays historical requests and measures hit/miss, token counts, latency, and kv-access patterns
Build recommendation engine that scores policy candidates by expected cost delta and regression risk
Integrate with config apply service: propose -> dry-run -> canary -> ramp -> full with rollback hooks
Create Console panel and monitoring queries for rollout KPIs
Run internal pilot on three customers/workloads and collect telemetry for model refinement
comments: 2026-02-16 Diego Ramirez: Initial scoping complete. Spoke with SREs (Aisha, Priya) about viable rollback metrics. We should avoid relying only on token-cost delta; quality (response truncation vs cache) needs a spot check via eval prompts.

2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Prototype forecasting (EWMA + trend) shows good short horizon accuracy for stable routes, but fails for bursty test routes. Will trial LSTM with per-prefix embedding features next sprint.

2026-02-28 Diego Ramirez: Design decision: keep candidate policy representation simple JSON with fields: key_template, ttl_seconds, shard_count, normalize_flags. This avoids heavy model coupling during apply time.

2026-03-03 Priya Nair (SRE): Review feedback: add isolation per dedicated pool to prevent cross-tenant eviction interaction. Also require that any TTL decrease must be accompanied by a rollback window >=24h.

2026-03-07 Aisha Patel: Simulator run #4 against 14-day historical window attached. Forecast suggests potential 18% token-savings for route text-gen-v2 with canonicalization and 8s TTL. However p95 predicted increase +6% for cold-start users - flag as medium risk.

2026-03-09 Diego Ramirez: Implemented canary orchestration prototype (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1492). Need tests for automated rollback triggers. Planning pilot on staging cluster next week.
2026-03-10 Design review (Jin Park): Recommend adding UX text explaining advisory confidence bands and 'why this recommendation' with a small CTA to preview simulated traffic impact in-console.
rollback_plan: If canary detects p95 latency > baseline+15% or errors > baseline*3 for 10m, automatically revert config to previous version; for ramp stage, pause and alert SREs and Product; full rollback requires audit log entry and runbook completion.
decision_log: Keep candidate policy as simple JSON to decouple from model internals and reduce blast radius during apply
Require 24h minimum rollback observation window for any TTL reduction to avoid rapid oscillation of cache size
Pilot on hosted API routes first; dedicated pool nuances (eviction interactions) will be handled by pool isolation flag
Prefer EWMA forecasting for short horizons and LSTM ensemble for bursty routes; ensemble only used when confidence interval tightens
notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive TTLs increase hit-rate initially but can amplify cold-start latency for infrequent prefixes. The adviser must expose risk scores and explainability to product owners.
Quality checks: tie selected prompt-level evals to any recommendation that affects >10% of a tenant's traffic. If eval shows >2% textual regression, recommendation is rejected.
Operational constraint: adviser must not add >200ms to request path in dry-run mode; heavy sim runs must be async and offloaded to batch workers.
